about: The alert rules of grafana/alerts/agent-alerts.yaml, for python -m obs alerts (windows counted in closed runs).

rules.title: A write timed out and nobody checked whether it happened
rules.first_step: Run `python -m obs find duplicate_write` (or the TraceQL query `duplicate write` in grafana/traceql.md), then ask the system that owns the write (payments for a refund, orders for a label or a reshipment) about each operation ID before anyone sends the change again.

rules.title: Replies to customers failed
rules.first_step: Open the example runs (`python -m obs trace RUN_ID`): did each ticket go to a person, or close as resolved? `python -m obs find no_action` lists the tickets closed without a reply. Send those replies when the reply service works again.

rules.title: Runs stopped by a loop limit
rules.first_step: Open three stopped runs (`python -m obs find loop`): which model, which step repeats? Compare with the last release.

rules.title: Cost per resolved ticket over budget
rules.first_step: Split the cost by model and slice (`python -m obs cost --by model`, the Cost panels): which change raised it? The budget (US$0.002 per resolved ticket) is an assumption: Omar's.

rules.title: Too many tickets handed to a person
rules.first_step: Split the handed-over runs by model (`python -m obs cost --by model --outcome handed_to_person`) and compare with the day before: a model or a release with many more handoffs is the first suspect. Open its example runs.
